BHP.policy_date: Approved by the Board of BHP Group Limited to take effect on 1 October 2024 (released to ASX 1 October 2024)
BHP.covered_persons: All BHP directors, employees and contractors (insider-trading prohibition). Additional tiers: persons on insider lists; participants in BHP employee incentive plans (excluding Shareplus); Restricted Persons (e.g. ELT members who are not PDMRs, their assistants/managers, Investor Relations, Group Governance, Asset Presidents, key Corporate Affairs/Group Reporting employees); PDMRs (directors of BHP Group Limited, KMP named in the Remuneration Report, anyone the Group Company Secretary determines to be a PDMR); and Persons Closely Associated (PCAs) with PDMRs.
BHP.closed_periods: For insider-list persons, Restricted Persons, PDMRs, PCAs and incentive plan participants: (1) from the end of BHP's financial year to publication of the full year results announcement; (2) from the end of BHP's half year to publication of the half year results; (3) any other period declared by the Board or the Disclosure Committee. Separately, 'Excluded Dealings' (DRP, SPP, rights issue, takeover/scheme/buy-back acceptance, no-change-in-beneficial-interest transfers) require clearance only during the 30 days prior to the full year results announcement and the 30 days prior to the half year results.

derivatives.detail: PDMRs (directors, KMP and persons so determined) are prohibited from transactions in put options, call options or other derivative securities, but the ban is expressly qualified to those 'on an exchange or in any other organised market'; an OTC bilateral derivative is not expressly banned, though it falls within the 'Dealing' definition (contract to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations; grant/acceptance/acquisition of any option) and so needs clearance and is barred in Closed Periods. No derivative ban applies to Restricted Persons or other staff.
derivatives.evidence: where the dealing involves transactions in put options, call options or other derivative securities, on an exchange or in any other organised market

hedging_unvested.detail: Employee incentive plan participants must not at any time enter a transaction that operates or is intended to operate to limit their exposure to the risk of holding unvested plan securities (or vested securities under holding locks). PDMRs are separately prohibited from using unvested BHP securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including hedging and margin loans.
hedging_unvested.evidence: Participants must not at any time enter into a transaction that operates or is intended to operate to limit participants' exposure to the risk of holding unvested BHP securities granted under a BHP employee incentive plan

hedging_vested.detail: The only express ban on hedging vested securities is for incentive plan participants in respect of 'vested BHP securities that are subject to holding locks or similar restrictions'. Hedging of unrestricted vested shares is not expressly prohibited; it is a 'Dealing' ('entry into a contract to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations'; options) so PDMRs, Restricted Persons and insider-list persons need written clearance, cannot deal in a Closed Period, and PDMRs remain subject to the exchange/organised-market derivatives ban and the one-year short-term dealing ban. The PDMR heading refers to 'no ... hedging' and BHP applies a 'substance over form approach'.
hedging_vested.evidence: or vested BHP securities that are subject to holding locks or similar restrictions

monetisation.detail: Forward sales, prepaid forwards, swaps and similar are not named, but the 'Dealing' definition captures any 'agreement to ... dispose of securities', 'entry into a contract to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations' and 'any other right or obligation, present or future, conditional or unconditional, to acquire or dispose of securities', so they require clearance for PDMRs/Restricted Persons/insider-list persons and are barred in Closed Periods; PDMR bans on short-term dealing (maturity of one year or less) and exchange/organised-market derivatives also apply.
monetisation.evidence: any other right or obligation, present or future, conditional or unconditional, to acquire or dispose of securities

short_selling.detail: PDMRs are prohibited from dealing where the dealing involves short selling BHP securities. Stock lending agreements are 'Dealings' for all covered persons. No short selling ban is stated for non-PDMRs.
short_selling.evidence: where the dealing involves short selling BHP securities (i.e. the practice of borrowing a security and selling it in the hope that it can be bought back at a lower price some time in the future to close out the short position)

margin_lending.detail: 'Entry into any margin lending or other secured financing arrangement' is a 'Dealing', so it requires clearance for PDMRs/Restricted Persons/insider-list persons and is barred in Closed Periods. PDMRs are additionally prohibited from using unvested BHP securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including hedging and margin loan arrangements (the section heading reads 'no short term dealing, short selling, margin loans or hedging').
margin_lending.evidence: where the dealing involves using unvested BHP securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including hedging and margin loan arrangements

encumbrance.detail: Granting security over BHP securities is a 'Dealing' for everyone covered ('use as security, or otherwise granting a charge, lien or other encumbrance over securities'), so PDMRs/Restricted Persons/insider-list persons need clearance and cannot do so in a Closed Period. No requirement that holdings remain unencumbered, except that PDMRs cannot use unvested securities as collateral.
encumbrance.evidence: use as security, or otherwise granting a charge, lien or other encumbrance over securities

short_term_trading.detail: PDMRs are prohibited from dealing in BHP securities on a short-term basis; an investment with a maturity of one year or less is considered short-term. Not stated for non-PDMRs.
short_term_trading.evidence: on a short-term basis. An investment with a maturity of one year or less is considered of a short-term nature

BHP.minimum_holding_period: No express minimum holding period; for PDMRs 'An investment with a maturity of one year or less is considered of a short-term nature' and is prohibited.

approval.approver: Group Company Secretary or their delegate (each a 'Clearance Officer') for persons on an insider list, Restricted Persons, PDMRs and PCAs (a PDMR may submit the form on behalf of a PCA); Clearance Officer responds in writing within two business days; clearance is discretionary, refusal is final and binding, and clearance can be withdrawn. Exceptional-circumstances determinations only by the Group Company Secretary or the Chair of the Board.
approval.validity: Dealing must be completed within two business days of receipt of written approval; clearance lapses if the person comes into possession of Inside Information and can be withdrawn on new information or change of circumstances.
approval.post_trade_notification: PDMRs and PCAs must immediately notify the Group Company Secretary of the transaction details after dealing; BHP notifies the UK FCA within three business days of the dealing and announces to relevant stock exchanges within two business days of being notified.
approval.evidence: Wait for written approval from the Group Company Secretary or their delegate (each a Clearance Officer) ... Upon receipt of written approval, the dealing must be completed within two business days.

exceptional_circumstances.detail: A PDMR (including PCAs) or Restricted Person may be cleared to deal during a Closed Period if not in possession of Inside Information and either exceptional circumstances (severe financial difficulty, court order) require the immediate sale of shares, the dealing is under or related to an employee incentive plan, or there is no change in beneficial interest. Only the Group Company Secretary or the Chair of the Board can determine severe financial difficulty/exceptional circumstances.
exceptional_circumstances.evidence: exceptional circumstances, such as severe financial difficulty or compulsion by court order, exist which require the immediate sale of shares

other_collar_relevant_clauses: 'BHP will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this policy when applying and enforcing it.'

'Dealing includes any transaction or change affecting title to or interest in securities, including: ... entry into a contract to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations; the grant, acceptance, acquisition, disposal, exercise or discharge of any option; ... use as security, or otherwise granting a charge, lien or other encumbrance over securities; ... entry into any margin lending or other secured financing arrangement.'

'securities means any publicly traded or quoted securities of any entity ... or any other financial products or instruments whether quoted or not and any securities that are convertible into or linked to such securities' - an OTC collar is a 'financial product ... whether quoted or not ... linked to' BHP shares.
'The purpose or motive for the dealing, or whether a profit is made from the dealing, is irrelevant.'

Section heading for PDMRs: 'Additional restrictions on PDMRs - no short term dealing, short selling, margin loans or hedging' (the body text bans only hedging/margin loans using unvested securities as collateral).

'Where clearance is required for a dealing under this policy, clearance will not be granted where the dealing would not satisfy the considerations above' (the 'front page of the newspaper' reputational test).

'Any clearance to deal can be given or refused by a Clearance Officer at their discretion.' / 'A decision to refuse clearance is final and binding.' / 'A clearance to deal can be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances.'
'If clearance is refused or an approval is revoked, the person seeking the clearance must keep that information confidential and not disclose it to anyone.'

PDMRs include 'any person determined by the Group Company Secretary to be a PDMR'; ELT members who are not PDMRs are 'Restricted Persons' and are not subject to the PDMR derivatives/short-term/short-selling/collateral bans.
PCAs of PDMRs (family members and controlled entities/trusts) are subject to the same clearance and Closed Period rules, so a collar written to a director's family trust is caught.
BHP.collar_assessment: A director or KMP (a PDMR) is not expressly prohibited from entering an OTC collar with a bank over vested, unrestricted BHP shares: the express derivatives ban covers only put/call options 'on an exchange or in any other organised market', and the express hedging bans cover unvested securities and vested securities 'subject to holding locks or similar restrictions'. The collar is nonetheless a 'Dealing' (a contract to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to price fluctuations, and the grant/acquisition of options), so it needs written clearance from the Group Company Secretary, must be executed within two business days of clearance, cannot occur in a Closed Period or while holding Inside Information, and must be notified immediately after dealing (with FCA/ASX disclosure). Risks: BHP's 'substance over form' approach and the PDMR heading 'no ... hedging' give the Clearance Officer discretion to refuse; a tenor of one year or less could breach the short-term dealing ban; any funded/secured leg cannot use unvested securities as collateral and is itself a further Dealing needing clearance. Restricted Persons and other employees face only the clearance/Closed Period rules and, if incentive plan participants, the ban on hedging unvested or holding-locked securities.

CBA.policy_date: Effective 1 October 2024 (version 10.0, approved 12/08/2024; released to ASX 1 October 2024)
CBA.covered_persons: Three tiers. (1) All employees, contractors, secondees and directors of CBA and subsidiaries (insider-trading ban; Pre-Clearance may apply). (2) 'Specified Persons' and their 'Associates' (spouse/partner, dependent children, co-resident relatives, family whose trading they control, controlled entities): Trading Windows, hedging of unvested/locked plan securities, margin lending, 30-day hold, CFD/short/stock-lending bans. Specified Persons include at a minimum CBA Board directors, Group Executives, Subsidiary Board directors, Group Company Secretaries and subsidiary company secretaries, Executive General Managers, their direct support staff and Group Control Room staff. (3) CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives and each of their Associates: additional ban on hedging any vested Group Securities and UK/EU MAR restriction. Pre-Clearance applies to the CBA Board, Group CEO, Group Executives and others designated in the Procedure/Conflicts Hub.

trading_windows.opens: day after the Group's half year results are released to the ASX
trading_windows.closes: 30 days after opening (orders may be placed until market close on the last day)

trading_windows.opens: day after the Group's full year results are released to the ASX
day after the Group's May trading update is released to the ASX
day after the Group's November trading update is released to the ASX
any one-off period as determined by the CBA Board, such as for new Securities issuances
trading_windows.closes: as determined by the CBA Board

CBA.closed_periods: Residual only: 'All other periods are closed periods' (cl 10). Specified Persons and Associates may only Trade in Group Securities during a Trading Window unless a cl 14 exception applies or an exceptional-circumstances approval is obtained under cl 15/Attachment A. The CBA Board may vary, suspend or close Trading Windows at any time.

derivatives.detail: Derivatives over Group Securities (expressly including OTC options, hedges and equity swaps) are themselves 'Securities'/'Group Securities', so for Specified Persons any derivative dealing is a 'Trade' that must occur in a Trading Window and be Pre-Cleared where Pre-Clearance applies. CFDs, short selling and stock lending are banned outright (cl 16(c)); any derivative that limits economic risk is banned for the top tier over all vested securities (cl 9) and for all Specified Persons over unvested or locked plan securities (cl 8).
derivatives.evidence: any derivatives products relating to the types of securities listed above, including but not limited to equity swaps, warrants, futures, contracts for difference, hedges and exchange traded or over the counter options, whether settled by cash or otherwise.

hedging_unvested.detail: All Specified Persons must not limit the economic risk of their exposure to Group Securities received under any Group equity plan that are unvested, or vested but still subject to a plan holding lock or trading restriction.
hedging_unvested.evidence: Specified Persons must not enter into a transaction that limits the economic risk of their exposure to Group Securities received under any Group equity plan that are: a. unvested; or b. vested but subject to a holding lock or trading restriction under the terms of the plan.

hedging_vested.detail: For CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives and each of their Associates, any transaction limiting economic risk on any vested Group Securities (plan-sourced or purchased) is banned; a purchased put is squarely a transaction that limits the economic risk. For other Specified Persons the ban covers only vested plan securities still under a holding lock/trading restriction; hedging of unrestricted vested shares by that tier is not expressly banned but is a Trade in a Group Security subject to the window, Pre-Clearance and cl 16 restrictions.
hedging_vested.evidence: In addition, the CBA Board directors, Group Company Secretaries, Group Executives, and each of their Associates, must not enter into a transaction that limits the economic risk of their exposure to any vested Group Securities.

monetisation.detail: Not expressly addressed by name. Forward sales, prepaid variable forwards and equity swaps are caught indirectly: 'Security' includes equity swaps and OTC options, 'Trade' includes agreeing to dispose, and any structure that transfers downside limits the economic risk and so is banned for the top tier under cl 9. Using the shares as collateral for a funded structure is separately banned by cl 16(a).
monetisation.evidence: must not enter into a transaction that limits the economic risk of their exposure to any vested Group Securities.

short_selling.detail: Specified Persons and Associates must not use any instrument or arrangement for short selling or stock lending of Group Securities, or enter CFDs, except to the extent covered by the cl 14 exceptions.
short_selling.evidence: enter into contracts for difference or use any instruments or enter any arrangements for short selling or stock lending of Group Securities, except to the extent covered by any of the "Exceptions to Trading Windows" in this Policy.

margin_lending.detail: Specified Persons and Associates must not use Group Securities as security for margin lending, the stated rationale being that a forced sale may breach the Policy.
margin_lending.evidence: use Group Securities as security for margin lending or other secured financing arrangements, as a forced sale may lead to the breach of this Policy;

encumbrance.detail: The same clause extends beyond margin loans to 'other secured financing arrangements', so pledging Group Securities as collateral for any financing (including the funding leg of a monetised collar) is banned for Specified Persons and Associates. No general 'must remain unencumbered' statement beyond this.
encumbrance.evidence: use Group Securities as security for margin lending or other secured financing arrangements

short_term_trading.detail: Specified Persons and Associates must not hold Group Securities for less than thirty days, calculated last-in-first-out; each new purchase restarts the 30-day clock. Conditional/limit/stop-loss orders must be both placed and executed within a Trading Window.
short_term_trading.evidence: hold Group Securities for less than a thirty-day period, calculated on a last in, first out basis

CBA.minimum_holding_period: 30 days, last-in-first-out basis (Specified Persons and Associates, cl 16(b))

approval.approver: Policy defers to the Group Personal Trading Procedure and Conflicts Hub. Attachment A identifies the Pre-Clearance approver for the top tier: CBA Board Chair for CBA Board directors (other than the Chair), the CEO and their Associates; Board Audit Committee Chair for the Board Chair and Associates; CEO for Group Executives and Associates. Trading Window exceptions for other tiers: relevant Subsidiary Board Chair/Deputy Chair; Group General Counsel and Group Executive Legal & Group Secretariat for other Specified Persons.
approval.validity: Pre-Clearance: three business days unless withdrawn earlier. Trading Window exception: seven calendar days unless revoked earlier (Pre-Clearance must be obtained within that period).
approval.post_trade_notification: Only for Trading Window exception trades: confirmation of whether the Trade has been placed to the approver and Group Control Room by no later than the next business day. General post-trade reporting is left to the Procedure.
approval.evidence: Pre-Clearance requirements apply to the CBA Group Board, Group CEO and Group Executives and certain other individuals as outlined in the Procedure and on the Conflicts Hub. ... Pre-Clearance will last for three business days unless withdrawn earlier.

exceptional_circumstances.detail: Specified Persons and Associates may apply in writing to the relevant approver to Trade outside a Trading Window in exceptional circumstances, e.g. severe financial hardship where a sale is the only practical method, a court order, or an overriding legal/regulatory transfer requirement. Decisions are final, may be refused without reasons, and the exception lasts seven calendar days. The hardship limb is framed around a sale, not a hedge.
exceptional_circumstances.evidence: severe financial hardship where the sale of Group Securities is the only practical method of overcoming hardship;

other_collar_relevant_clauses: 'Trade or Trading includes buying, selling, acquiring, transferring or disposing of Securities, agreeing to do so, or procuring someone else to do so, whether on or off market.' Entering an OTC collar (and writing a call, i.e. agreeing to dispose on exercise) is itself a Trade.

'Group Security' includes both vested and unvested Securities and, via 'Security', 'hedges and exchange traded or over the counter options, whether settled by cash or otherwise'. A cash-settled collar is still a Group Security.

'Trading involving conditional or limit orders ... must be placed and executed during a Trading Window.' The cl 14 exceptions contain no carve-out for exercise or settlement of a pre-existing derivative.
'Pre-Clearance or an exception being granted is not an endorsement of any Trade.'

'Specified Persons must make their Associates aware of the requirements of this Policy and take reasonable steps to ensure their Associates comply.' A collar in a spouse's or family trust's name is caught.
Top tier must not Trade any other Security whose price or value depends on a Group Security listed or traded on a UK or EU regulated market (cl 18, MAR).

'Any other requests for exemptions from this Policy should be made in accordance with the Group Policy Framework.' Exemption Authority: Group Chief Risk Officer. The only route around cl 9, with no stated criteria.
Group Securities include PERLS capital notes, ASB perpetual preference shares, and ETFs with 20% or more CBA weighting.
Off-market transfers with no change in beneficial ownership are exempt from windows 'other than those by the CBA Board directors and their Associates'.
CBA.collar_assessment: For a CBA Board director, Group Executive or Group Company Secretary (or any of their Associates), a collar over vested CBA shares is not available: cl 9 bans any transaction that limits the economic risk of their exposure to any vested Group Securities, which a purchased put does regardless of the written call or whether the structure is funded, and cl 16(a) independently bars using the shares as security for any financing leg. The only theoretical path is an exemption from the Group Chief Risk Officer under the Group Policy Framework, for which the policy gives no criteria. A lower-tier Specified Person (e.g. an EGM or subsidiary director) holding vested shares not under a plan holding lock is outside cl 8/9, but the collar is a Trade in a Group Security that must be entered in a Trading Window with Pre-Clearance where required (valid three business days), cannot involve stock lending, CFDs or secured financing, is subject to the 30-day LIFO hold, and has no window exception for exercise or settlement of the option legs.

WBC.policy_date: Undated in the policy body; released to ASX as a revised policy on 5 February 2021
WBC.covered_persons: Section 3 (insider trading, unvested hedging ban, short-term trading ban) applies to all Westpac Directors, directors of controlled entities, and all employees, secondees and contractors in Australia and overseas. Section 4 (blackouts, notification/approval, margin loans, short selling, blackout exceptions) applies only to Westpac Directors and Prescribed Employees (including Group Executives and Key Prescribed Employees). Both extend to 'associates' and 'employee related accounts' (spouse/partner, dependent children, family trusts, controlled companies, entities of which the person is a director/secretary/executive officer).
WBC.closed_periods: Two Blackout Periods: (1) from 15 March until the beginning of trading in Sydney one day after announcement of half-year results in early May; (2) from 15 September until the beginning of trading in Sydney one day after announcement of full-year results in early November. The Chief Compliance Officer may extend or reduce these, conditionally or unconditionally.

derivatives.detail: 'Securities' expressly includes derivatives and options, so insider trading and Blackout Period rules apply to them. Options/derivatives that limit economic risk on unvested holdings are prohibited for everyone; over vested holdings they are not prohibited but, for Directors and Prescribed Employees, are subject to the Section 4 approval/notification/pre-clearance regime for 'hedging arrangements over vested Westpac securities'.
derivatives.evidence: You must not enter into any options, derivatives or other arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding in Westpac securities ... This prohibition does not apply to vested holdings in Westpac securities, although approval or notification and other arrangements apply to Directors and Prescribed Employees dealing in vested securities

hedging_unvested.detail: All Directors and Employees (Section 3 applies group-wide) are prohibited from any option, derivative or other arrangement that limits the economic risk of unvested Westpac securities or unvested entitlements under employee share plans.
hedging_unvested.evidence: You must not enter into any options, derivatives or other arrangements which operate to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding in Westpac securities or other unvested entitlements under employee share plans.

hedging_vested.detail: Hedging vested holdings is expressly not prohibited. Outside a Blackout Period, Westpac Directors need the Chairman's prior approval (Chairman of the Board Audit Committee for the Chairman) and must notify the Company Secretary immediately afterwards; Prescribed Employees must lodge a Trade Notification Form beforehand; Key Prescribed Employees must obtain pre-clearance under the separate Key Prescribed Employee Trading Process. No hedging of vested securities is permitted during a Blackout Period or while holding inside information.
hedging_vested.evidence: Westpac Directors must obtain the approval of the Chairman before they or their associates do any of the following outside a Blackout Period: buy or sell Westpac securities, or entering into a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities

monetisation.detail: Forward sales, prepaid variable forwards, equity swaps and funded/monetised structures are not mentioned. The closest hooks are the 'hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities' approval/notification trigger and the rule that any transaction causing a change in ownership is a 'trade', which would capture any physical delivery or transfer leg.
monetisation.evidence: Any transaction which causes a change in ownership of Westpac securities will be considered a trade of securities under this Policy.

short_selling.detail: Short selling (selling borrowed financial products) by Westpac Directors and Prescribed Employees is prohibited and treated as a breach. The clause is in Section 4 so it applies to that tier, not to all employees.
short_selling.evidence: Short selling by Westpac Directors and Prescribed Employees is prohibited and will be considered a breach of this Policy.

margin_lending.detail: Directors and Prescribed Employees may take margin loans over Westpac securities, but margin calls may not be met by selling Westpac securities during a Blackout Period or while holding inside information; a lender sale in a Blackout Period is a breach regardless of instruction. Persons are expected to be able to meet calls without selling and are steered toward facilities without price triggers. Key Prescribed Employees must disclose margin lending arrangements to the Group Control Room.
margin_lending.evidence: Westpac Directors and Prescribed Employees are permitted to take out margin loans over their holdings in Westpac securities, however margin calls are not to be met by the sale of Westpac securities at a time when they would not be permitted to trade Westpac securities under this Policy.

encumbrance.detail: There is no general rule on pledging, granting security or keeping holdings unencumbered; the only encumbrance treated is a margin loan (permitted, with the sale restrictions above). A bank taking security over the collared shares is therefore not expressly regulated except to the extent it involves a margin facility or a lender-forced sale.
encumbrance.evidence: If your margin lender sells any of your Westpac securities during a Blackout Period, whether on your instructions to do so or not, it will be considered a breach of this Policy.

short_term_trading.detail: Short-term or speculative trading (entry to exit within a few days to a few weeks) is prohibited group-wide; all employees must trade with a medium to long-term perspective. A loss-avoiding early sale may be possible with Group Control Room guidance.
short_term_trading.evidence: Short-term or speculative trading is prohibited and all employees must conduct their personal trading activities with a medium to long term perspective.

approval.approver: Chairman for Westpac Directors (Chairman of the Board Audit Committee for the Chairman); pre-clearance under the Key Prescribed Employee Trading Process (an Addendum not included in the document) for Key Prescribed Employees; other Prescribed Employees need only give prior notification to the Group Control Room via the online Prescribed Employee Trade Notification Form.
approval.post_trade_notification: Westpac Directors must notify the General Manager, Company Secretary immediately of any trading by themselves or associates, including entering into a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities. Directors or Group Executives granted a Blackout Period exception must advise the Group General Counsel & Enterprise Executive and the Company Secretary to assist with any Appendix 3Y.
approval.evidence: Westpac Directors must obtain the approval of the Chairman before they or their associates do any of the following outside a Blackout Period: buy or sell Westpac securities, or entering into a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities ... Westpac Directors must also notify the General Manager, Company Secretary immediately of any trading

exceptional_circumstances.detail: Directors and Prescribed Employees facing an unreasonable financial impost or other exceptional circumstances may apply in writing (Directors to the Chairman; Chairman to the Chairman of the Board Audit Committee; Group Executives, Key Prescribed and Prescribed Employees to the Group General Counsel & Enterprise Executive) for an exemption from the ban on selling in a Blackout Period. The exception is framed around a sale or disposal only, not hedging, and the decision-maker must decline if they hold inside information.
exceptional_circumstances.evidence: Westpac Directors and Prescribed Employees who have an unreasonable financial impost or who are in other exceptional circumstances may apply in writing to be exempted from the prohibition on selling Westpac securities during a Blackout Period.

other_collar_relevant_clauses: 'Securities' include ... derivatives; or options; or ... any other financial products that are able to be traded on a financial market (s3.2) - a collar is therefore a 'security' for blackout and insider trading purposes.

The prohibition on hedging is limited to arrangements which 'operate to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding in Westpac securities or other unvested entitlements under employee share plans' (s3.4); it 'does not apply to vested holdings'.

Trigger wording for Directors and Prescribed Employees is 'entering into a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities' or 'arrange for another person to enter into arrangements of those kinds' (ss4.4, 4.6) - so both the executive and an associate/trust entering the collar are caught.

'Any transaction which causes a change in ownership of Westpac securities will be considered a trade of securities under this Policy' (s4.4) - physical settlement, delivery to the bank at expiry, or transfer of shares into a custody/security structure could each be a 'trade' needing separate approval or notification and must not fall in a Blackout Period.

Key Prescribed Employees 'are subject to the requirements as set out in the Key Prescribed Employee Trading Process, which is an Addendum to this Policy' (s4.2) - the addendum is not part of the published document, so pre-clearance mechanics for senior executives cannot be verified from this text.

Chief Compliance Officer 'has discretion to impose ad hoc restrictions at times when matters subject to ASX Listing Rule 3.1A are being considered' (s4.3) - an ad hoc restriction could prevent entry, roll or unwind of a collar.

Margin calls 'are not to be met by the sale of Westpac securities' in a Blackout Period; persons 'should take steps to rearrange their affairs to have a facility that does not contain price triggers' (s4.8) - relevant if the collar is funded or the bank takes security with price-triggered enforcement.
Short-term trading ban (s3.5) requires 'a medium to long term perspective' - a short-dated collar or one unwound within weeks could be characterised as speculative.
Directors 'should seek guidance from the Group General Counsel & Enterprise Executive or the General Manager, Company Secretary' (s6).
WBC.collar_assessment: Yes, in principle. Section 3.4 expressly carves vested holdings out of the derivatives/hedging ban, and Sections 4.4-4.6 contemplate 'entering into a hedging arrangement over vested Westpac securities', so a purchased put / written call over vested shares is a contemplated transaction. A Westpac Director must first obtain the Chairman's approval (or the Chairman of the Board Audit Committee if the Chairman) and then notify the Company Secretary immediately; a Key Prescribed Employee (most senior executives) needs pre-clearance under an unpublished addendum; other Prescribed Employees only need to lodge a prior notification. The collar cannot be entered, rolled or physically settled during either Blackout Period (15 March to post-half-year results; 15 September to post-full-year results) or under an ad hoc restriction, and the collar must not cover any unvested shares or unvested plan entitlements. Monetisation and security/encumbrance are not addressed, so any funded leg should be structured to avoid margin-style price-triggered sales and any share transfer to the bank should be treated as a separate 'trade'.

MQG.policy_date: Last review / last updated 2 January 2024; released to ASX 2 January 2024 as 'updated effective January 2024'
MQG.covered_persons: All 'Macquarie Staff', defined to include Staff (employees, agency workers, interns, secondees, contractors/consultants as deemed by RMG Employee Compliance), Key Management Personnel (all Voting Directors and members of the Executive Committee of MGL) and Associates (spouse/partner, dependants under 18, relatives in the same household, and any person whose investment decisions Staff may influence). Additional restrictions apply to KMP and 'Executive Directors' (undefined term) in ss 2.2.3 and 2.4.

trading_windows.closes: Up to five weeks after release, subject to Macquarie's discretion
Up to five weeks after release, subject to Macquarie's discretion
Up to five weeks after the AGM, subject to Macquarie's discretion

trading_windows.opens: Other specific periods where Macquarie has publicly released all relevant price-sensitive information (at Macquarie's discretion)

MQG.closed_periods: Not framed as closed periods: all dealing outside a Staff Trading Window is 'strictly prohibited' unless an Excluded Dealing (s 1.3) or an exceptional-circumstances waiver (s 2.3). Windows are 'a conditional exception to the general prohibition on trading, rather than permission to trade'.

derivatives.detail: Derivatives are not separately regulated but are brought inside the definition of 'Macquarie securities', so any dealing in options, warrants, futures or structured products over MQG is subject to the same regime: only during a Staff Trading Window and only with pre-clearance (or by exceptional-circumstances waiver).
derivatives.evidence: Macquarie securities Includes, but is not limited to: ... Structured products providing exposure to MQG shares, including but not limited to ETFs; Futures contracts, options and warrants over MQG shares

hedging_unvested.detail: All Macquarie Staff are prohibited at any time (including inside a window) from entering any transaction designed or intended to hedge exposure to Macquarie securities that are unvested or subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction. No approval route is provided.
hedging_unvested.evidence: Macquarie Staff are not permitted at any time to enter into a transaction that is designed or intended to hedge their exposure to Macquarie securities which have not vested or are subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction.

hedging_vested.detail: Hedging of 'unrestricted' Macquarie securities is expressly allowed subject to pre-clearance and the general personal dealing requirements (i.e. inside a Staff Trading Window); for KMP it is additionally subject to the s 2.4 financing-arrangement disclosure regime. Overlay: KMP and Executive Directors may not enter a transaction that limits or reduces the economic risk of their shareholding below the minimum personal shareholding requirement.
hedging_vested.evidence: They can however enter into a transaction intended to hedge unrestricted Macquarie securities subject to pre-clearance and other general personal dealing requirements (and, in respect of Key Management Personnel, subject to section 2.4 below). Key Management Personnel and Executive Directors may not enter into a transaction that operates to limit or reduce the economic risk of their shareholding below the minimum personal shareholding requirement.

monetisation.detail: Forward sales, prepaid variable forwards and equity swaps are not named. They are captured by (a) the broad 'dealing' concept (transfers of beneficial ownership, 'entering into an agreement to trade'), (b) the s 2.2.3 hedging clause where the structure is designed to hedge, and (c) the 'margin loans or other financing arrangements' provisions (ss 2.2.2, 2.4) where the structure is funded. Net effect: allowed over unrestricted securities only, with pre-clearance, in a window, and for KMP subject to s 2.4 disclosure and the minimum-shareholding floor.
monetisation.evidence: Macquarie considers dealing to include, without limitation, securities transactions such as transfers of beneficial ownership and trading (either directly or indirectly), including entering into an agreement to trade.

short_selling.detail: Uncovered short selling of any security including Macquarie securities is prohibited for all Macquarie Staff even when a window is open. Covered short selling is not addressed.
short_selling.evidence: Macquarie Staff are prohibited from engaging in short-term trading and uncovered short selling arrangements in relation to any security, include a Macquarie security (even if the designated Staff Trading Window is open).

margin_lending.detail: Margin loans and other financing arrangements over Macquarie securities are permitted for all Staff with a 'should' obligation to hold sufficient cash or collateral to meet margin calls. For KMP: annual disclosure of financing arrangements to Macquarie, immediate notification to the Company Secretary in the listed circumstances, and pre-clearance (via PTA) before liquidating a position to satisfy a margin call.
margin_lending.evidence: Macquarie Staff who enter into margin loans or other financing arrangements over Macquarie securities should ensure they have sufficient available cash or other acceptable collateral to meet margin calls including during a period of extreme sudden market downturn.

encumbrance.detail: No prohibition on lending, mortgaging or charging Macquarie securities and no requirement that holdings remain unencumbered. KMP must immediately inform the Company Secretary if they hold Macquarie securities that have been lent, mortgaged or charged to a financier, if the financier is or is likely to become entitled to demand payment, or if a demand could not be met without disposing of at least 1% of issued securities.
encumbrance.evidence: KMP must inform the Company Secretary immediately if the following circumstances apply: the member of KMP holds Macquarie securities that have been lent, mortgaged, or charged to a financier

short_term_trading.detail: Short-term trading in any security including Macquarie securities is prohibited for all Macquarie Staff even inside a window. 'Short-term' is not defined.
short_term_trading.evidence: Macquarie Staff are prohibited from engaging in short-term trading and uncovered short selling arrangements in relation to any security, include a Macquarie security (even if the designated Staff Trading Window is open).

approval.approver: Pre-clearance is obtained through Macquarie's conflicts management systems / the PTA personal compliance system (administered by RMG Employee Compliance), plus any additional business group approval; exceptional-circumstances waivers are approved by the ANZ Regional Head of Compliance, Global Head of Compliance or Head of Risk Management Group on written request to RMG Employee Compliance.
approval.validity: All pre-clearances are 'subject to an expiry date' (period not stated) and may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or circumstances change; waivers likewise.
approval.post_trade_notification: None for ordinary dealings. KMP must annually disclose financing arrangements relating to their Macquarie securities and must inform the Company Secretary immediately if securities are lent, mortgaged or charged to a financier (and in the other s 2.4 circumstances).
approval.evidence: Dealing in Macquarie securities by Macquarie Staff must be pre-cleared against Macquarie's conflicts management systems. ... All pre-clearances are subject to an expiry date and may be withdrawn if new information comes to light or there is a change in circumstances. A denied pre-clearance is final and binding on the Macquarie Staff member who made the request and must be kept confidential.

exceptional_circumstances.detail: A specific waiver to deal outside a Staff Trading Window may be granted for compulsion of law/regulation, severe financial hardship, or other circumstances deemed exceptional. Written request to RMG Employee Compliance with a statutory declaration that the dealing is the only reasonable action available and the person holds no non-public price-sensitive information; approval by the ANZ Regional Head of Compliance, Global Head of Compliance or Head of RMG; absolute discretion, expiry date, refusal final and confidential.
exceptional_circumstances.evidence: A specific waiver from the prohibitions on dealing in a Macquarie security outside a Staff Trading Window may be granted in exceptional circumstances. Exceptional circumstances include where a Macquarie Staff member may need to deal in a Macquarie security: by compulsion of law or regulation ... on account of severe financial hardship.

other_collar_relevant_clauses: s 1.1: 'Macquarie considers dealing to include, without limitation, securities transactions such as transfers of beneficial ownership and trading (either directly or indirectly), including entering into an agreement to trade.' Entering an OTC collar is therefore a 'dealing' and must occur in a Staff Trading Window with pre-clearance.

s 2.1: 'Dealing in a Macquarie security outside a Staff Trading Window by Macquarie Staff is strictly prohibited unless it is an Excluded Dealing (refer to section 1.3 above) or exceptional circumstance (refer to section 2.3 below).' A collar is not an Excluded Dealing.

s 2.2: 'Macquarie Staff may also be subject to additional business group or jurisdictional specific requirements and must consult their business group policy for details.' and the Policy 'should be read in conjunction with the Macquarie Personal Investments Policy' (not provided).

s 2.2.3: hedging of KMP holdings is expressly made 'subject to section 2.4', so a KMP collar is treated as a financing arrangement for disclosure purposes: 'KMP must annually disclose their financing arrangements relating to their Macquarie securities to Macquarie.'
s 2.4: 'Liquidating a position to satisfy a margin call requires pre-clearance against Macquarie's PTA system.' Relevant where a funded collar has a margin/collateral top-up mechanism.

s 2.4: KMP must inform the Company Secretary immediately where 'circumstances have arisen in which the financier is entitled or likely to become entitled to exercise a right under the finance arrangements to demand payment' or where a demand could not be met 'without the disposal of securities representing at least 1% of the total number of issued securities of Macquarie'.

s 3.1 'Associates': the collar restrictions extend to the executive's spouse/partner, dependants, co-resident relatives and any person whose investment decisions the executive may influence (e.g. family trusts/companies).

s 1.1: insider-trading overlay applies 'even if the designated Staff Trading Window is open'; and s 2.2: 'Where pre-clearance is received and business group approval provided, Macquarie Staff must satisfy themselves that the relevant dealing is appropriate and that they do not hold any non-public, price-sensitive information'.
MQG.collar_assessment: Yes, in principle. The policy expressly permits transactions 'intended to hedge unrestricted Macquarie securities' subject to pre-clearance (via the PTA/conflicts system, plus any business group approval) and the general dealing rules, so the collar must be entered into during a Staff Trading Window (up to five weeks after interim results, final results or the AGM) and cannot cover any shares that are unvested or subject to a holding lock or dealing restriction (including MEREP RSUs/DSUs/PSUs). For a KMP (Voting Director or Executive Committee member) or an 'Executive Director', the collar must not limit or reduce economic risk on the shareholding below the minimum personal shareholding requirement (set outside this policy), and a KMP must disclose the arrangement annually and notify the Company Secretary immediately if the shares are lent, mortgaged or charged to the bank or the bank becomes entitled to demand payment. Collars, monetisation structures and 'written' clearance are not expressly addressed, and the Personal Investments Policy and business group policies (not provided) may add requirements.

ORG.policy_date: Effective from 11 March 2025 (lodged with ASX 11 March 2025; next review due 11 March 2028)
ORG.covered_persons: All Origin Directors, employees and people working for Origin under a contract or consultancy agreement ('Origin Personnel'), extended to their Associates (spouse/de facto, dependent children, controlled or significantly influenced companies/partnerships/trusts, and persons acting in concert).
ORG.closed_periods: From 1 July to the second trading day after the announcement of Origin's results for the financial year ended 30 June; and from 1 January to the second trading day after the announcement of Origin's results for the half financial year ended 31 December. Plus any confidential 'Additional Prohibition' imposed by the Company Secretary with the CEO.

derivatives.detail: Derivatives and financial products over Origin Securities are expressly within the definition of 'Dealing' (and 'Securities' includes options, any financial product and derivatives), so they are subject to the same closed-period prohibition, prior written clearance and other restrictions as share trades; they are not separately banned.
derivatives.evidence: Dealings or arrangements to: buy or sell Securities or financial products issued or created over, or in respect of Securities; ... create a derivative over Securities; ... or enter into an agreement to do any of the above

hedging_unvested.detail: All Origin Personnel are prohibited from dealing in instruments or financial products that limit the economic risk of equity-incentive securities while they are subject to performance hurdles or otherwise unvested.
hedging_unvested.evidence: You must not Deal in instruments or other financial products which operate to limit the economic risk of any Securities issued to you under any equity incentive schemes provided by Origin while those holdings are subject to performance hurdles or are otherwise unvested.

hedging_vested.detail: Hedging of incentive securities after vesting is expressly contemplated and permitted provided it complies with the Policy (outside Closed Periods/Additional Prohibitions, no Inside Information, prior written clearance, no secured financing). Hedging of non-incentive vested holdings is not separately addressed but falls within 'Dealing' via the derivative/financial product limbs.
hedging_vested.evidence: Any sale, hedging arrangement or other Dealing involving those Securities after they have vested must be done in compliance with this Policy.

monetisation.detail: Forward sales, swaps and similar structures are not named, but 'Dealing' captures agreements to buy or sell Securities or financial products over them, so they require clearance and are barred in Closed Periods; a funded/prepaid structure secured over the shares would additionally be caught by the ban on 'any other secured financing arrangements in respect of Origin Securities'.
monetisation.evidence: enter into an agreement to do any of the above

short_selling.detail: Absolute ban on short selling Origin Securities for all Origin Personnel.
short_selling.evidence: You must not engage in short-selling Origin Securities.

margin_lending.detail: From 11 March 2025 all Origin Personnel are prohibited from entering margin lending arrangements using Origin Securities (solely or in a portfolio) as collateral; a forced sale by a margin lender in a Closed Period is a serious breach that may result in dismissal.
margin_lending.evidence: you must not enter into margin lending arrangements using Origin Securities (either solely or as part of a portfolio) as security as a collateral against repayment of a loan

encumbrance.detail: Prospective ban (from the date of the Policy) on entering any secured financing arrangement in respect of Origin Securities; there is no express standalone requirement that holdings remain unencumbered and non-financing security interests are not addressed.
encumbrance.evidence: or enter into any other secured financing arrangements in respect of Origin Securities.

short_term_trading.detail: No short-term or speculative dealing; no acquiring with intention to dispose within three months; no arrangements that result in short-term Dealing (margin loans given as example). Carve-out for securities acquired on exercise of options/rights or shares acquired under employee equity incentive schemes.
short_term_trading.evidence: You must not acquire Origin's Securities with the intention of disposing or selling them within three months of acquisition, or enter into arrangements which result in short-term Dealing (such as margin loans)

ORG.minimum_holding_period: 3 months (intention-based; does not apply to securities acquired under Origin's employee equity incentive schemes)

approval.approver: Directors: Chairman and the Company Secretary; ELT & ELT Direct Reports: Manager and the Company Secretary; all other employees: Manager. (Clearance for the Chairman is not addressed.)
approval.validity: Transaction should be completed within 2 business days of receiving clearance and must be consistent with the terms of the clearance; clearance is void if Inside Information is obtained after clearance.
approval.post_trade_notification: Directors only: confirmation of price and quantity must be provided to the Company Secretary following a Dealing (no deadline stated).
approval.evidence: you must comply with the prior written clearance requirement set out below before you can Deal ... Any transaction should be completed within 2 business days of receiving clearance and must be consistent with the terms of that clearance.

exceptional_circumstances.detail: No severe-financial-hardship or other exceptional-circumstances exception; dealing in a Closed Period or Additional Prohibition is flatly not permitted.
exceptional_circumstances.evidence: Dealing in Origin Securities during a Closed Period or Additional Prohibitions will not be permitted.

other_collar_relevant_clauses: 'Securities' includes 'options; any financial product; derivatives', so the put and call legs of a collar are themselves Origin Securities and any later unwind, roll or close-out is a fresh Dealing.
If you come to possess Inside Information after receiving clearance to Deal, you must not complete the trade.

A sale of your Origin Securities by a third party outside your control (such as a margin lender) in a Closed Period or when you are otherwise prohibited by this Policy is a serious breach of this Policy and may result in dismissal.
General exception where 'the transaction results in no change in the beneficial interest in the Securities' is drafted for transfers to super funds etc.; not a safe basis for a derivative overlay.
Additional Prohibitions are confidential: you may be told that a prohibition exists, but not told why or for how long it will last.
Exercise of incentive options/rights is a permitted dealing 'but not any other Dealing of Securities following exercise'.
Clearance 'is not an endorsement of the proposed Dealing'.
ORG.collar_assessment: A director or executive can enter an OTC collar over vested Origin shares: hedging is only banned while incentive securities are unvested, and post-vesting hedging is expressly permitted in compliance with the Policy. Conditions: no Inside Information; outside the 1 July and 1 January Closed Periods and any confidential Additional Prohibition; prior written clearance (Directors: Chairman and Company Secretary; ELT and direct reports: Manager and Company Secretary) with the trade executed within 2 business days on the cleared terms; Directors must confirm price and quantity afterwards. A funded or monetised collar is problematic: any loan secured over the shares is caught by the ban on any other secured financing arrangements, and the structure must not permit a bank-initiated sale during a Closed Period. Each unwind, roll or close-out is a separate Dealing requiring fresh clearance.

WTC.policy_date: Dated 16 October 2021; effective from 1 November 2021 (lodged with ASX 2 November 2021)
WTC.covered_persons: All Directors and Group employees ('Employees'). A 'Restricted Persons' tier (Directors; senior management team as defined by the CEO; others who regularly possess inside information and have been advised by the Company Secretary) is subject to additional section 5 restrictions (blackouts, notification/approval, margin lending). Restricted Persons must also take steps in relation to dealings by persons over whom they have investment control or influence.
WTC.closed_periods: For Restricted Persons only: from close of trading on 30 June until and including the day of the ASX announcement of full-year results; from close of trading on 31 December until and including the day of the half-year results announcement; any other period the Board specifies. All Employees must also not deal when the Company notifies them not to (s 4.1).

derivatives.detail: No clause expressly addresses options, warrants or other derivatives. Touchpoints are the insider-trading description of 'deal' (entering an agreement to buy or sell, exercising options), forward contracts named as short-term dealings in s 4.2, and the broad hedging definition in s 4.3.
derivatives.evidence: buy or sell securities in a company, or enter in an agreement to buy or sell securities, or exercise options over securities, or otherwise apply for, acquire or dispose of securities (deal)

hedging_unvested.detail: Applies to all Employees. Securities acquired under a Company equity plan must never be hedged before vesting; hedging is any arrangement that limits the economic risk of holding Company securities.
hedging_unvested.evidence: Company securities acquired under an employee or director equity plan operated by the Company must never be hedged prior to vesting.

hedging_vested.detail: The hedging ban is confined to pre-vesting securities and securities under a holding lock or plan dealing restriction; vested, unlocked shares are not caught by s 4.3. A collar is an arrangement limiting economic risk and, on the s 3 'deal' description and the forward-contract example, likely a dealing: for Restricted Persons it is subject to blackouts, prior notification (Directors) or approval (other Restricted Persons), the 6-month short-term rule and the substance-over-form clause; other Employees are subject only to ss 4.1 and 4.2.
hedging_vested.evidence: Company securities must never be hedged while they are subject to a holding lock or restriction on dealing under the terms of an employee or director equity plan operated by the Company.

monetisation.detail: Forward sales, prepaid variable forwards and swaps are not expressly addressed. Forward contracts are named only as an example of a prohibited short-term dealing under the 6-month rule, and any structure that limits economic risk is hedging for s 4.3.
monetisation.evidence: entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts)

short_selling.detail: All Employees must not deal on a speculative basis, which expressly includes short selling.
short_selling.evidence: Employees must not deal in the Company's securities on a speculative basis, including short selling.

margin_lending.detail: Entering a margin lending arrangement over Company securities, or transferring Company securities into an existing margin loan account, requires prior approval via the s 5.5 written Clearance to Trade process. The Company may impose conditions, e.g. on when securities may be sold to meet a margin call. A disposal by a secured lender exercising its rights is an Excluded Dealing (s 6(e)).
margin_lending.evidence: Approval must be obtained in accordance with the procedure set out in section 5.5 for any: 1) entering into a margin lending arrangement in respect of the Company's securities; and 2) transferring securities in the Company into an existing margin loan account.

encumbrance.detail: No general prohibition on pledging or encumbering securities and no requirement that holdings be unencumbered; the policy addresses only margin lending (approval) and disposals by a secured lender (excluded dealing).
encumbrance.evidence: a disposal of securities of the Company that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement.

short_term_trading.detail: All Employees must not deal on a short-term basis, defined to include buying and selling on market within a 6 month period and other short-term dealings such as forward contracts. Selling shares received on vesting within 6 months of vesting is carved out.
short_term_trading.evidence: Short-term trading includes buying and selling securities on market within a 6 month period, and entering into other short term dealings (for example, forward contracts).

WTC.minimum_holding_period: 6 months in effect (buying and selling on market within 6 months is short-term trading); shares received on vesting may be sold within 6 months of vesting.

approval.approver: Directors: prior notification (not approval) to the Company Secretary and the Chair of the Board (Chair of the Audit & Risk Committee for the Chair). Restricted Persons other than Directors: prior approval via a Clearance to Trade Request Form to the Company Secretary; the policy refers to 'the approver' without naming the office. Margin lending (s 5.6) and exceptional-circumstances dealing (s 5.2) use the same s 5.5 process. Non-Restricted Employees: no clearance required.
approval.validity: Approval: dealing should occur within 5 business days following approval (or such other time specified), otherwise fresh approval is required; approval may be revoked at any time. Director notification: may deal for 5 business days following notification.
approval.post_trade_notification: Directors and other key management personnel must promptly notify the Company Secretary following any trade, ideally by close of business on the day the trade is entered into.
approval.evidence: you must complete a "Clearance to Trade Request Form" and submit it to the Company Secretary ... the approved dealing should occur within 5 business days following approval (or such other time specified in the approval), otherwise the approval is no longer effective

exceptional_circumstances.detail: A Restricted Person not in possession of inside information may apply to deal in a blackout period in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship or court-order compulsion) with sufficient evidence that the dealing is the most reasonable course of action.
exceptional_circumstances.evidence: Exceptional circumstances are likely to include severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order.

other_collar_relevant_clauses: s 1: The Company will take a substance over form approach and will have regard to the intent and spirit of this Policy when applying and enforcing it.
s 2: Restricted Persons must also take steps in relation to dealings by persons over whom they have, or are deemed to have, investment control or influence.
s 4.3: Hedging is entering into any arrangements that operate to limit the economic risk associated with holding the Company's securities.
s 5.3: By notifying their intention to deal, the Director is taken to have satisfied themselves that the proposed dealing is within the terms of this Securities Trading Policy.
s 5.5: the approver may impose conditions on the dealing in their discretion, is not obliged to provide reasons and may revoke their approval at any time.
s 5.6(b): margin lending approval may be conditional upon such terms and conditions as the Company sees fit (for example, the circumstances in which securities may be sold to satisfy a margin call).
s 6(a): where plan securities cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any dealings in those securities must only occur in accordance with this Policy.

s 6(d): exclusion for trading under a pre-approved non-discretionary trading plan not entered or amended in a blackout, with no discretion and not cancellable in a blackout other than in exceptional circumstances.
s 6(e): exclusion for a disposal of securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example under a margin lending arrangement.
WTC.collar_assessment: A collar over vested shares no longer subject to a holding lock or plan restriction is not prohibited: the s 4.3 hedging ban is limited to pre-vesting securities and securities under a plan holding lock, and there is no derivatives, monetisation or general encumbrance prohibition. Given the 'deal' description, the forward-contract reference and the substance-over-form clause, the collar should be treated as a dealing: a Director must give prior notification to the Company Secretary and the Chair (or ARC Chair) and execute within 5 business days; a non-Director Restricted Person needs written clearance (5 business days, revocable, conditions may be imposed); execution must be outside the 30 June and 31 December blackouts and any Board-specified blackout, and the Director or KMP must notify the Company Secretary by close of business on trade date. A funded collar (loan secured over the shares) likely needs s 5.6 margin lending approval on a substance-over-form reading, and a collar with tenor under 6 months, or over shares bought on market within the last 6 months, risks the short-term dealing prohibition.
